newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Residents rejoice as Zaire rebels take Kikwit town.
newsitem.headline: Residents rejoice as Zaire rebels take Kikwit town.

text.p: Rebels seized control of Zaire's provincial town of Kikwit on Tuesday and thousands of people poured into the streets in jubilation, residents said.
"Rebels entered at 6 a.m. (0500 GMT)," said one resident in radio contact with the capital Kinshasa 400 km (250 miles) away. "Now the population is jubilating in the streets."

Residents said the rebels, mostly teenagers but including some adults, all spoke English, Swahili or Portuguese. English and Swahili are the common languages of Laurent Kabila's Tutsi-led guerrilla army. There have been widespread reports of support for the rebels from Portuguese-speaking Angola.
Government soldiers retreated from Kikwit, the most important town between the rebel front line and Kinshasa, on Monday, the residents said.
"They entered like a knife through butter," a resident said, adding that there was no fighting or shooting.

A government spokesman in the capital said the army had not yet received confirmation of Kikwit's fall to rebels, who control more than half the vast Central African nation and are closing in on the capital.
